To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the parotid gland is a common site of metastatic spread for melanomas and squam-ous cell carcinomas of head and neck sites, and the incidence of parotid gland metastases is higher than previously reported in the literature.

1) the parotid lymph node metastases are more common in patients with advanced stages of the disease and in those patients with a history of neck dissection; 2) the presence of parotid gland lymph node metastases is a poor prognostic sign; 3) the presence of metastases in the parotid gland is associated with a high incidence of neck node metastases and distant metastases.
The parotid lymph nodes drain the skin of the face and neck, the oral cavity and the nasal cavity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of parotid gland in the metastatic spread of cancer.
the development of new and improved methods for the diagnosis and therapy of cancer.
the study of the parotid gland as a metastatic site for neoplasms of the upper aeridigestive tract and skin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the parotid gland can be a site for primary neoplasia, metastasis from a regional or distant site, or both.
metastatic disease to the parotid gland is a rare event.
the parotid gland is not a primary site for any neoplasm but can be the site of metastases from regional and distant sites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parotid gland tumors can be benign or malignant, and the treatment for each is quite different.
we have demonstrated that there is no single, unique pattern of metastatic spread to the parotid gland or its lymph nodes.
the parotid lymph nodes are a common metastatic site from cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, but not from cutaneous melanoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parotid lymph node is a metastatic site for a number of different cancers, but that the most common cancers that metastasize to the parotid are head and neck cancers and breast cancer.
the parotid lymph nodes are not a metastatic site for the majority of primary tumors in the head and neck.
parotid lymph node metastases are associated with a poorer prognosis than primary parotid gland tumors, and that this is independent of the histological grade of the parotid lymph nodes.
